messages:
anne: quick sync — PRD draft for scoped tokens + org/project RBAC is up. need acceptance criteria, edge cases, and rollout notes. PTAL

mike: link?

anne: https://internal.redwood/prd/scoped-tokens (draft)

sarah: skimmed. couple customer asks from Enterprise A: must support token-scoping by project_id, role=read-only, and binding to service accounts.

julian: perf note: token introspection could be hot. caching at auth proxy and cached TTL needed.

anne: proposing acceptance criteria (draft):
- AC1: minting API accepts {org_id, project_id, roles[]} and returns a scoped token tied to those IDs.
- AC2: token verification returns scope attrs and resolves to allow/deny decision within 15ms p95 for hosted API.
- AC3: scoped tokens are immutable after issuance; any project_id reassignments do NOT change existing tokens.
- AC4: deletion of a project triggers token invalidation within 60s (via revocation index).
- AC5: audit log emitted for mint/revoke/verify with token_id, actor_id, org_id, project_id.
- AC6: default TTLs: short-lived (24h) for third-party service tokens, long-lived (90d) for org-admin tokens; configurable per org.

mike: edge cases to call out:
- project deleted but token still presented (stale resource) -> ensure 403 and clear log entry.
- token minted with role that later gets removed from RBAC matrix -> how to handle? deny at verify-time if role absent.
- org owner rotates keys -> how to map existing API keys vs new scoped tokens.

sarah: customer ask: must be able to mint tokens scoped to multiple projects in same org (multi-project access). is that allowed? security teams will push back but some product teams need it.

julian: multi-project scope ok but increases introspection complexity. suggest single token carry a list of project_ids up to N=10 and require indexing in revocation store.

anne: migration note: existing API keys map to org-level tokens. migration flow in PRD:
1) create org token for each legacy key, mark as migrated.
2) emit notice to owner and set expiry window.
3) allow owners to replace with scoped tokens.

mike: operational reqs:
- revocation store must support 100k ops/s for large customers.
- introspection cache invalidation when role matrix changes.

sarah: acceptance criteria addition:
- AC7: when RBAC role definitions change, system enforces new role set on subsequent verifies; logging of any denied verifies due to role drift.

julian: implementation details suggestion:
- token payload minimal: token_id, org_id, project_ids[], roles[], exp, iat.
- store full metadata in internal token-store for audit + revocation.
- use bloom filter for quick revoked-token checks plus hot KV for precise revocations.

deploy-bot: RFC created: rfc/1827005432-scoped-token-authz.md by anne

mike: prioritization: enterprise sales flagged as blocker for 2 customers. recommend target in next milestone (sprint+1) as high priority.
sarah: +1 but require a migration playbook and admin UI to list issued tokens per project.

anne: noted. I'll add migration playbook section and mockups for admin UI in PRD.
julian: follow-ups for infra: rollout canary by org, collect metrics: auth_latency_p95, token_revocations/sec, 401_by_org. set alerts for auth_latency_p95 > 25ms.

anne: outstanding questions to resolve before RFC->PRD merge:
- exact TTL defaults and org-overrides policy
- multi-project token limits and representation
- project-deletion invalidation window (60s vs eventual)
- migration cadence for legacy API keys

mike: i'll loop in sales to gather which customers need multi-project tokens.
sarah: i'll add security review checklist and sign-off gate for enterprise launch.

anne: thanks all — i'll update the draft with ACs, edge-case decisions, and rollout plan, then ping for final review. :thumbsup:
